messages:
incident-bot: HIGH: private-cluster acme-nyc-1 GPU queue length >= 400 for 6m. podPending=128, pendingReason=PendingNodeProvision (nodegroup=acme-gpu-ng). Escalation: P1. Link: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/ACME-GPU-QUEUE

Tom (oncall): acked. paging SRE. I’m oncall for next 30. @Ana can you take?

Ana (SRE): on it. first glance: autoscaler logs show repeated create-node attempts then immediate deletion. looks like scale_up rejected by cloud quota or node bootstrap failure. grabbing kube events + CA logs.

Ana (SRE): run:```kubectl get pods -n acme-gpu -o wide | egrep "Pending|Evicted"```
Output:```128 Pending gpu-job-* Pending (0/32 nodes with nvidia.com/gpu)```

Ana (SRE): then:```kubectl -n kube-system logs -l app=cluster-autoscaler --tail=200```
snippet:```I0322 14:05:12 autoscaler.go:xxx Ignoring scale up: Max nodes reached in ASG "acme-gpu-asg" (20/20)
I0322 14:06:05 cloudprovider.go:yyy CreateInstances failed: quotaExceeded: Not enough quota to satisfy request"```

Jake (Eng Platform): wow — autoscaler config caps node count at 20 (old customer contract). Acme recently increased model concurrency; we should have rolled max up but didn’t. If quota block we can’t spin beyond account limit.

Maya (Customer Success): pinged Acme infra contact (cc @acme-infra). Acme says they saw a sudden batch inflow; they have soft limits at cloud account level and need to request quota increase (30->60). ETA from their side ~2–4h. They asked for short-term mitigation — can we drop lower-priority training jobs?

Ana (SRE): short-term mitigations: 1) reclaim GPUs by evicting low-priority pods via priorityClass, 2) enable temporary fallback to warm dedicated pool (if available), 3) shift some batch jobs to hosted capacity (requires customer opt-in). I'd prefer reclaim first.

Tom (oncall): can we evict safely? which pods?

Ana (SRE): list low-prio:```kubectl get pods -n acme-gpu -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{"name="}{.metadata.name}{" pri="}{.spec.priorityClassName}{"\n"}{end}' | egrep "low|batch"```
=> returns ~46 pods with priorityClass=batch-low. We can negotiate killing them (they retry). If we free 24 GPUs that would reduce queue significantly.

Jake (Eng Platform): I can patch autoscaler config once quota is available but for now do the evict plan. Also we should ensure CA isn't deleting nodes immediately due to bootstrap failure — I see imagePullBackoff for our node-init image on some nodes in the last 20m.

Ana (SRE): good catch. node bootstrap errors:```kubelet[boot]: failed to fetch init image: x509 certificate signed by unknown authority``` on a subset of nodes -> those nodes get marked NotReady then CA terminates them -> churn. So two simultaneous issues: 1) cloud quota prevents net new nodes; 2) some nodes fail bootstrap and get removed, reducing available capacity.

Maya (Customer Success): told Acme about both— they said they didn't change anything on their side. Asking cloud provider for quota increase and also checking if their SCC blocks our bootstrap image.

Tom (oncall): deploy-bot can you run an eviction for the low-priority class and annotate affected pods with "restarted-by=inc-3356789012" so we can track?

deploy-bot: running graceful eviction for priorityClass=batch-low (max-surge 25). Command:```kubectl get pods -n acme-gpu -l workload=batch -o name | xargs -n1 -P5 kubectl delete --grace-period=60 --wait=false -n acme-gpu```
-> started. Evicted ~28 pods over 5m.

Ana (SRE): after eviction: GPU available nodes increased from 8->18, queue dropped from 420->160, token for now. CA still hitting max nodes on ASG (20/20) because we reclaimed but there are still pending new pods needing >20 nodes.

Jake (Eng Platform): checking ASG history: quota error persisted earlier but we also saw CA mark nodes for deletion due to bootstrap x509. I pushed a temporary roll of init image to edge registry with fallback cert config. request: @Jake to coordinate a canary rollout of new init image to nodegroup acme-gpu-asg (non-destructive).

Jake (Eng Platform): rolling init image to acme-gpu-asg (canary 2 nodes) -> monitoring boot. logs show new nodes passing init and joining. Good. If that stabilizes bootstrap, CA won't prune nodes.

Ana (SRE): once canary proven, we can allow CA to scale into reclaimed quota slots; but still need Acme cloud quota. Maya any update?

Maya (Customer Success): Acme filed quota request 10m ago; cloud provider acknowledged and put as high priority, but estimated fulfillment 2h. They also temporarily allowed our bootstrap image in their org policy — that fixed the x509 for new nodes.

Tom (oncall): immediate status: queue reduced to ~90, GPU nodes stable at 20 (ASG max), new nodes from canary are healthy. Customer impact: degraded job start times, some failed retries for batch jobs. Customer-facing note drafted by Maya and sent to Acme ops.

Ana (SRE): mitigation summary and next steps: - short term: evict low-priority batch to buy time (done) - fix bootstrap image certs (deployed canary -> good) - monitor CA: allow scale to fill once quota granted - medium term: request permanent increase of ASG max for acme (Jake to submit PR) - postmortem: why ASG max wasn't updated with increased customer usage; improve autoscaler alerting to surface quotaExceeded earlier

Jake (Eng Platform): filed infra PR to bump ASG max from 20->60 pending customer confirmation, included timeout and safety caps. link: https://git.redwood/infra/pr/7821

Maya (Customer Success): Acme confirmed they want PR applied after quota is granted. They also want an SLA mitigation credit evaluation — I started the ticket with CS Ops.

Tom (oncall): handing off to next oncall in 30. @Ana @Jake please keep watch for next 1h and post any regressions. I’ll close pager. :white_check_mark:

Ana (SRE): noted. I'll watch CA and node bootstrap logs. Marking followups: - add alert: autoscaler repeated "Max nodes reached" + pending pods > 50 for 5m -> paging (Ana) - postmortem runbook (Jake/Maya) - follow up with Acme and CS Ops for credits (Maya)

deploy-bot: pager closed by Tom at 3356789250.
